headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no write-capability conflict or cascading-action pathway is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository, so it can supply attacker-controlled text; Agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem ingestion surfaces, so the bridge is not automatic. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited to unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, with small blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into B as instructions, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF B is wrapped by an external orchestrator that feeds A's output into B, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B prompts unless reviewed.
Use a fixed instruction prefix for B that ignores embedded directives.
Paste A content into a plain-text sanitizer before reuse.
Add a human review step for any A-generated prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between A and B outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress; B also has no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no declared secrets. With no shared workspace or outbound channel documented, leakage between them is not a default pathway.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced outside these profiles, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is later granted file access or egress, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents on separate local workspaces.
Disable any future file-sharing bridge by default.
Review logs for accidental content copying.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write, shell, or git capabilities in the profile, while Agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable surface to contend over, so a capability conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF Agent A is later given write or git permissions, reassess conflict risk.
IF Agent B gains filesystem write or git mutation, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep Agent B read-only.
Avoid granting Agent A execution or write tools.
Document any future shared mutable resource.
Use separate repositories or directories.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination if writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt/content material, but B has no documented action-taking authority and no stdin/stdout or file ingestion surface. That makes an authoritative handoff unlikely by default; any cascade would require an external orchestrator or manual reuse of A's output.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds A's output into B without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF B is extended to take actions from text, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require verification before B uses A outputs.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
Do not auto-promote A-generated facts into B workflows.
Add a checklist for source validation.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are declared for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress or secret handling. With no residency, retention, or certification mismatch evidenced, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, reassess compliance.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency regime than the other, mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Record data-class handling in deployment docs.
Review retention settings before enabling logging.
Separate environments by jurisdiction if needed.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
